Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

lawyer noun

also attorney, solicitor, barrister, advocate, counsel, defence lawyer, defense lawyer, counsellor, counselor, trial lawyer, appoint an attorney, serve at the bar, practise law

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.212
Cic. Mur. 25 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 192, 196
Levi–Bini p. 37

jūriscōnsultus, jūriscōnsultī m.

noun, second declension

lawyer, legal expert

One skilled in the law, who gave opinions, pleaded and drew up documents (Cic. de Or. 1.212). Also written as two words, jūris cōnsultus.

Other words

  • advocātus, advocātī m. — advocate: the lawyer who speaks for someone in court

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Quint. 12.1.13 (Lewis & Short); Plin. Ep. 7.22 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 167, 196; Traupman 338

    In Cicero’s day a friend called in to stand by a party with advice; from Quintilian on, the pleader himself (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s lawyer for the defence.

  • patrōnus, patrōnī m. — the advocate who pleads a case

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.51; Cic. Rosc. Am. 5: huic causae patrōnus exstitī (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word for the speaker who defends a client in court; also a patron or protector.

  • causidicus, causidicī m. — pleader

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.202 (Lewis & Short); Quint. 12.1.25 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 338; Traupman 167, 196, 398

    Often contemptuous: the mere pleader, as against the true orator (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s trial lawyer.

  • cognitor, cognitōris m. — an attorney acting for a party

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. cognitor: “an advocate, attorney (acting in the name of the parties)”; Traupman 193; Lewis & Short; Traupman 274

  • jūrisperītus, jūrisperītī m. — a legal expert, a counsellor

    often written as two words, jūris perītus · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 81: et jūris et litterārum … bene perītus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 194; Traupman 297; Traupman 338

  • dēfēnsor, dēfēnsōris m. — the counsel for the defence

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. dēfēnsor II; Traupman 190, 194; Traupman 302

  • āctor causārum — a trial lawyer, a pleader

    also used · classical · Traupman 197

Examples

  • Sīn autem quaererētur quisnam jūris cōnsultus vērē nōminārētur, eum dīcerem, quī lēgum et cōnsuētūdinis ejus, quā prīvātī in cīvitāte ūterentur, et ad respondendum et ad agendum et ad cavendum perītus esset

    But if it were asked who truly deserves the name of lawyer, I would say the man who is skilled in the laws and in the customs that private citizens follow in the state, at giving opinions, at pleading and at drawing up documentsCic. de Or. 1.212

  • Jūdicis est semper in causīs vērum sequī, patrōnī nōn numquam vērī simile, etiam sī minus sit vērum, dēfendere

    It is always the judge’s part in a trial to follow the truth; the advocate’s, sometimes, to defend what looks like the truth, even if it is less trueCic. Off. 2.51

  • cognitōrem alicui adscrībere

    to appoint an attorney for someoneTraupman 193

  • in jūdiciīs versārī

    to practise at the barTraupman 193

  • in forō agere

    to practise at the barTraupman 193

  • Dēsīderō jūriscōnsultum. Potesne mihi succurrere?

    I need a lawyer. Can you help me?Traupman 192

See also court, trial, case, law.
